area.reviews.1.quote: Our furnace had been making this annoying scratching/grating noise since last winter, and when it started doing it every time the heat kicked on a few weeks ago, we finally called C&S. Rob came by and said the motor was on its last leg - he said we could replace the motor or the whole furnace and gave us pricing for both.
area.reviews.2.quote: Great service all around! Carissa was polite and promptly scheduled my appointment. Rob came over and answered all of my questions thoroughly. The pricing was reasonable, so we decided to replace the AC and Furnace at the same time. We are so happy that we chose to do both at once! We were surprised that it was such a quick process to update everything.
area.reviews.3.quote: Three times, my experience with Suburban Heating and Cooling has exceeded my expectations. The first time I found them as a quick search, my heat went out on a Saturday morning. He was here at 9am that day to fix it. Kind, prompt, and knowledgeable. He explained what he was doing, what he thought about my old furnace, and we agreed to keep fixing it.
area.reviews.4.quote: I’ve been using this company for over 9 years. Rob is always prompt, professional, reasonably priced and impeccably honest and respectful of costs and fairness. I’ve recommended them to countless friends. I’m known for finding and recommending quality contractors, I’m the Angie’s list of our friends group. When I say someone is quality my friends know they are. Cannot recommend highly enough.
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a bungalow, a post-war house and a shop
area.scope.1.why: Skokie's 1920s bungalows and flats can still run boilers and radiators; most post-war houses heat with a furnace.
area.scope.2.why: Bungalows and flats heated by radiators have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.3.why: In Skokie's two- and three-flats, one boiler can heat every unit, so the owners decide on repairs together.
area.scope.4.why: Bungalow furnaces sit in basements; many post-war houses keep the furnace in a first-floor utility room.
area.scope.5.why: Shops and restaurants on Dempster and Oakton run rooftop units and kitchen exhaust, so roof access and opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Skokie building
area.buildings.1.title: Post-war house
area.buildings.1.body: A furnace with central air, in the basement or a utility room. The condenser sits beside the house.
area.buildings.2.title: Brick bungalow
area.buildings.2.body: Often a boiler and radiators, sometimes converted to forced air. Ductless is a common way to cool.
area.buildings.3.title: Two- or three-flat
area.buildings.3.body: A boiler for the building or a furnace per unit. Condensers off the alley or on the roof.
area.buildings.4.title: Storefront or restaurant
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units, with kitchen exhaust and make-up air for the restaurants on Dempster and Oakton.

area.faq.heading: Skokie HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the furnace in my post-war house worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Skokie from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Can you work on the boiler in a 1920s Skokie bungalow?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Skokie need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the furnace has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace, boiler or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a two- or three-flat, tell us which units share the boiler.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Skokie is on our service area list, about 8 miles north of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Boiler service is on our list: pressure, circulators, zone valves and venting, in vintage two-flats and older houses.
extras.faq.4.a: It depends on the job. The Village of Skokie sets its own permit rules, mostly for installs and replacements. A repair or tune-up is a different job, so ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.
